h20-edgardo-rafael-baez.occupation: Attorney; U.S. Army veteran and former intensive care unit nurse
h20-edgardo-rafael-baez.summary: Edgardo Rafael Báez is a San Antonio attorney who was born in Ponce, Puerto Rico. He served in the U.S. Army as a combat medic, paratrooper and drill sergeant, and later worked as an intensive care unit nurse. In his first run for office, he won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary for Texas' 20th Congressional District without an opponent, and he will face Democratic incumbent Joaquin Castro on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot.

positions.stance: Wants to bring the federal deficit down to 3% of GDP or less by 2030 through spending cuts and revenue measures. Opposes broad stimulus such as $2,000 tariff rebate checks, which he compares to COVID-era stimulus that he says drove inflation.

Supports reforming Social Security and Medicare to deal with projected trust fund shortfalls. Lists options such as raising retirement ages, means-testing benefits, or slowing entitlement growth without raising taxes.

Wants Congress to put border security, interior enforcement and the protection of American workers first. Opposes amnesty and any path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants. Also proposes a merit-based legal immigration system tied to workforce needs.
Opposes closing the Dilley Immigration Processing Center. He argues that cutting detention capacity without stronger border security would not solve the problem.
Wants to change the Affordable Care Act without large subsidies, which he says mainly benefit big insurance companies. Supports an open market where people can choose from many health plans.
Names public safety as a top priority, citing violent and property crime rates, homelessness and repeat offending among young people in the district.
Calls for better reading and math programs and points to F-rated schools in the district. Says schools are teaching 'doctrines' instead of core subjects like English, math and science.

Says he has written 11 bills to introduce if elected, including veterans-related legislation. Said he was undecided on the Major Richard Star Act and the Take Care of America's Veterans Act until he could review where the funding goes.

Would support or introduce War Powers Resolutions requiring Congress to approve further military action. Would use appropriations to withhold money for unauthorized operations, and would back bipartisan legislation barring funds to occupy or annex Greenland.
